checked.found: Wikipedia and the Egyptian Museum put the start of construction under Senusret I (reigned 1971-1926 BCE). A column fragment of Intef II is older, so 1971 BCE marks the start of major building, not the first royal work.

Wikipedia gives c. 1264 BC for the start, about twenty years of work to 1244 BC. World History Encyclopedia allows 1264-1244 or 1244-1224 BCE, so the date is approximate. Four seated colossi of Ramesses II, about 20 m tall, flank the entrance.
Britannica: completed and the gold-and-ivory Athena dedicated in 438 BCE; exterior decoration continued to 432. Doric temple to Athena Parthenos on the Acropolis.
Founded in 622 CE after the Hijra; palm trunks and mud-brick walls; rebuilt by al-Walid I from 706 and enlarged many times since.
Wikipedia: begun 785 on the orders of Abd al-Rahman I. Smarthistory says 786 and another source 784/5, so 785 is the usual figure. Two-tier horseshoe arches.
Consecrated 28 December 1065; Edward the Confessor died 4-5 January 1066, about a week later; later the coronation church.
First stone laid 9 September 1296 to Arnolfo di Cambio's design; polychrome marble facing; Brunelleschi's dome finished 1436 (about 140 years later).
Built 1555-1561 for Ivan IV, commemorating the capture of Kazan (1552); a Russian source gives 29 June 1561. Britannica says c. 1560, so 1561 is the commonly cited year.

Britannica and the London Museum say construction finished in 1710, when Wren's son placed the final stone. Parliament formally declared it finished on 25 December 1711. The description does not say 'declared', so 1710 holds. The old cathedral was lost in the 1666 fire and Wren lived to 1723.
Cornerstone laid 19 March 1882 under del Villar; Gaudí took over in 1883 (some sources say 1884).
Cornerstones laid 6 April 1853; dedicated 6 April 1893 (forty years). Six spires. The Church site calls the stone quartz monzonite, while its newsroom says granite.
Rebuilt 1906-1907, so 1907 holds. The mosque is on the Bani River floodplain, not the Niger. (Already applied by the coordinator.)
checked.suggestion: Builders raised the world's largest mud-brick building on the Bani River floodplain, its walls bristling with wooden beams.

checked.found: Consecrated 25 May 1962 beside the ruins of the old cathedral bombed in 1940; Spence kept the ruins as a garden of remembrance; reconciliation symbolism.
Completed 1993. The 210 m minaret is now second to Algiers (265 m), so 'taller than any other' was out of date. (Already applied by the coordinator.)
checked.suggestion: A huge mosque rose on a rock above the Atlantic at Casablanca, with one of the tallest minarets in the world.

checked.found: Opened to the public 20 December 2007 after Eid al-Adha prayers; the official site counts 82 domes; construction began 1996.

Fire in April 2019 destroyed the spire and two-thirds of the roof. Official reopening 7 December 2024, first Mass 8 December. Some exterior spire work continued after reopening, which the description does not contradict.
